correctness.rationale: Necessity is witnessed by two explicit unresolved edge pairs: omitting two vertices of \(X\) makes \(ax\) and \(ay\) indistinguishable, while omitting one \(x_0\) and selecting no path vertex makes \(ax_0\) and \(ap_1\) indistinguishable. Sufficiency is proved by explicit distance signatures for the two allowed cases, including the only possible cross-type collision at the first path edge. Counting those disjoint cases gives the enumerator, minimum degree, basis count, total count, and basis-membership statements. An exhaustive direct-definition checker over 7,440 subsets for \(3\le k\le6\) and \(1\le\ell\le5\) reproduces every criterion and coefficient. The finite check supports but does not replace the all-orders proof.

value.rationale: Lollipop graphs are a standard dense-core/sparse-tail family, and the theorem gives a natural complete classification rather than only a scalar dimension. The factorized enumerator records every feasible edge-resolving set, the exact basis count grows with the tail length even though the edge metric dimension does not, and the basis family pinpoints the attachment vertex as uniquely absent from every minimum basis. This exposes structural information invisible in the scalar invariant and directly connects the family to current questions about edge-basis membership.
